constellations.source: Walker delta 1600/32/1; Walker delta 1600/32/7; Walker delta 1000/20/3; Walker star 800/16/1

leo-pnt-mega-shell.label: MODELLED - two-body Keplerian orbits (optional secular J2) around a spherical body, geometric visibility above an elevation mask, all-in-view dilution of precision with one receiver clock per constellation unless clock = "common"; no signal power, health or terrain. The Walker geometry and the published presets are checked against the Galileo OS SDD, the GLONASS ICD and the GPS SPS Performance Standard slot tables, and the GPS baseline global DOP statistics against SPS PS Appendix B (see docs/VERIFICATION-MATRIX.md)

body.mu_km3_s2.note: gravitational parameter of the central body (crate::body)

body.radius_km.note: reference radius of the central body (crate::body)

body.rotation_rate_deg_s.note: sidereal spin rate of the central body (crate::body)

constellations[].mean_visible.note: area-weighted mean over the grid and the window of this constellation's satellites above the mask

constellations[].shells[].altitude_km.note: semi-major axis minus the body radius

constellations[].shells[].inclination_de.note: orbital inclination to the body equator

constellations[].shells[].phase_offset_d.note: mean-anomaly offset between corresponding satellites of adjacent planes: 360*F/T

constellations[].shells[].phasing.note: Walker F: inter-plane phasing factor in 0..P

constellations[].shells[].planes.note: Walker P: equally spaced orbital planes

constellations[].shells[].raan_spacing_d.note: node spacing between adjacent planes: 360/P for a delta pattern, 180/P for a star

constellations[].shells[].total.note: Walker T: satellites in the shell

mars-orbit-pnt.label: MODELLED: two-body relay orbits with J2 secular drift, geometric visibility, Gaussian range noise and an instantaneous measurement model around a body from the published constants; not validated against a mission's navigation data. The Earth-to-body geometry inherits the solar-system ephemeris labels.

body.gm_m3_s2.note: central body's gravitational parameter GM, cited in body.rs

body.j2.note: central body's unnormalised J2 where one is carried; drives the relay and user secular drift

body.j2_reference_radius_m.note: the radius the J2 value is referenced to

body.radius_mean_m.note: central body's mean radius: the occultation sphere and the surface

body.sidereal_rotation_period_h.note: 360 degrees over the IAU prime-meridian rate; negative for retrograde rotation

earth_to_body.one_way_light_time_s.note: Newtonian light time from the body (retarded) to the Earth at the epoch

earth_to_body.one_way_range_m.note: speed of light times the one-way light time

earth_to_body.shapiro_delay_s.note: the Sun's one-way Shapiro delay on the Earth-to-body path

earth_to_body.sun_separation_deg.note: Sun-Earth-body angle at the Earth; small near a solar conjunction, where plasma and Shapiro delay grow

earth_to_body.two_way_range_m.note: round-trip path length received at the epoch

epoch.jd_tdb.note: scenario epoch as a Julian date in Barycentric Dynamical Time (TDB)

epochs[].error_relays_m.note: position error of the seeded Gauss-Newton fix, constellation only

epochs[].error_with_earth_m.note: position error of the seeded Gauss-Newton fix with the Earth range

epochs[].formal_sigma_relays_m.note: formal one-sigma position uncertainty from the weighted relay geometry

epochs[].formal_sigma_with_earth_m.note: formal one-sigma position uncertainty with the clock-free Earth row added

epochs[].n_relays_visible.note: relays whose line of sight clears the body (and the mask, for a surface user)

epochs[].user_radius_m.note: user distance from the body's centre

fom.availability_relays.note: fraction of epochs with a converged constellation-only fix (at least four relays)

fom.availability_with_earth.note: fraction of epochs with a converged fix once the Earth range is added

fom.earth_visibility.note: fraction of epochs the Earth is above the body's limb for the user

fom.mean_relays_visible.note: mean number of relays in view

fom.median_formal_sigma_relays_m.note: median formal one-sigma position uncertainty, constellation only

fom.median_formal_sigma_with_earth_m.note: median formal one-sigma position uncertainty with the Earth range

fom.median_pdop.note: median constellation-only position dilution of precision over epochs with four or more relays

fom.rms_error_relays_m.note: root-mean-square position error of the seeded constellation-only fixes

fom.rms_error_with_earth_m.note: root-mean-square position error of the seeded fixes with the Earth range

fom.rms_normalised_error_relays.note: root-mean-square of fix error over formal sigma, constellation only; near 1 when noise and covariance agree

fom.rms_normalised_error_with_earth.note: root-mean-square of fix error over formal sigma with the Earth range

n_relays.note: navigation satellites in the Walker pattern

relay_altitude_m.note: relay altitude above the mean radius

relay_period_s.note: two-body period of the relay orbit, 2 pi sqrt(a^3/GM)

sigma_earth_range_m.note: one-sigma one-way range noise of the two-way Earth measurement

sigma_relay_range_m.note: one-sigma pseudorange noise of a relay measurement

campaign-shared-jammer-sea-road.title: One jammer, a ship and a car
campaign-shared-jammer-sea-road.label: MODELLED composition of existing scenario kinds. Every number is read from a real run of the named kind; the chaining (additive carry of a channel across a phase boundary, zero-order hold onto the timeline grid, a phase ended at a computed time) is a modelling choice, and each phase carries the label of the kind that produced it.
